title: Compatible primitive-root coordinates for signed point Tate lines
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraic closure of a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. On $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ use the roots sheaves [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], the sectionwise inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], and the signed twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. There exists a sequence of primitive roots $\zeta_r\in k$ of order $\ell^r$, $r\ge1$, satisfying $\zeta_{r+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_r$. For every such sequence the maps
$$ (\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,s},\qquad j\longmapsto\zeta_r^j $$
are isomorphisms of sheaves, compatible with reduction of labels and the power transitions on roots, on every object of the pro-etale site. Their inverse limit sends $1$ to $e=(\zeta_r)_r$ and identifies $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,s}$ with $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_s$. Write $B_s=(A_{E,n})_s$ for $B=A_{E,n}$, and $B_s=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ for $B=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $e_B=e\otimes1$, $e_{0,B}=1$, $e_{m,B}=e_B^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and let $e_{-r,B}$ be the functional with $e_{-r,B}(e_{r,B})=1$ for $r>0$. For every integer $m$ the map $B_s\to B(m)_s$, $b\mapsto b e_{m,B}$, is an isomorphism of sheaves of $B_s$-modules. The inverse for a positive tensor line takes $b e_{r,B}$ to $b$, and the inverse for its dual takes $\varphi$ to $\varphi(e_{r,B})$. Under these coordinates, $\Gamma(s,B_s)=B$ and $\Gamma(s,B(m)_s)=B e_{m,B}$.

proof.text: Construct the primitive l-th root using lem-sc-primitive-root in the algebraic closure. Recursively take l-th roots. The order criterion for a prime power proves that the nth chosen root has order l^(n+1), since raising it to l^n gives the initial nontrivial root. This is pointRootTower.

For a prescribed compatible tower, transport the chosen roots through the affine global-sections isomorphism. Distinct powers have unit differences. Reuse the explicit constantRootsIso construction of lem-poincare-compatible-primitive-roots and the rawRootIso and moduleIsoOfAddIso constructions of lem-pur-twist-root-local-models. Naturality of the constant-sheaf comparison and sheafification units gives exactly the stated exponentiation formula, including empty and disconnected objects.

Reuse rootsBasisIso and the actual/coefficient diagram comparisons to identify the full root and residue towers. Its components are the preceding finite coordinates. Naturality proves compatibility with transition maps. The completedBasis construction and its projection formula from lem-pur-twist-root-local-models identify the inverse limits, retaining the completed coefficient action. Restriction over the terminal object gives the global module isomorphism.

Extend the completed root coordinates along the completed scalar map. The normalized scalarExtensionUnitIso of lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence and the integralExtensionReverse construction of lem-pur-twist-integral-local-models give integral coordinates sending 1 to the prescribed tensor. Extend once more along the finite completed projection and compose with integralFiniteIso. The units in the quotientTensorAdjunction and the ordinary tensor adjunction commute with their unique left-adjoint comparison; evaluating this equality on x proves that the finite comparison sends 1 tensor x to the ordinary discrete quotient tensor 1 tensor x.

Use the identity in degree zero. Recursively tensor the positive coordinate isomorphisms, using the normalized tensor left unitor and the functoriality in both factors. Their pure-tensor formulas show that the next generator is the tensor of the preceding generator with the degree-one generator. Linearity and the two isomorphism identities give the prescribed scalar and positive-inverse formulas.

Define the dual generator on each localized site by the inverse of the positive coordinate map on every object. A local functional is its scalar multiple by its value on the positive generator, by naturality and linearity. This gives an explicit linear bijection from the coefficient sheaf to internal Hom, whose inverse is evaluation at the identity object. The negative generator evaluates to 1.

Specialize the ring-isomorphism clause of lem-pur-connected-adic-integral-basis to the connected scheme Spec k and the identity extension E/E. Reuse its finiteConstantEquiv for the finite coefficient ring. These are normalized by the stated constant maps. Compose their underlying bijections with evaluation of each signed module-sheaf isomorphism at the terminal object.
